title: Catena template source
description: One hand-edited template definition: the Portainer App Template fields a human owns, plus the x-catena extension block carrying everything the Portainer format has no slot for (SSO wiring, backup quiesce hooks, bench membership, sizing, bilingual prose). sources/<id>.json is canonical; templates.json, catalog.json, blueprints/ and index.html are generated from it. An entry the registry importer wrote carries x-catena.status "imported": it publishes with stubs where a curated entry has hand-written parts, and the published catalog marks it untested.

id.description: Stable slug. MUST equal the filename stem. Used as the blueprint directory, the sentinel key, and the id every consumer joins on.

type.description: Portainer template type. 2 = swarm stack deployed from a git repository. Every Catena template is a swarm stack: the client host already runs a single-node swarm carrying the catena services, so a compose stack would be a second runtime beside it with none of the placement or restart policy the rest of the box is held to.

name.description: Stack name Portainer prefills on deploy.

categories.description: Filter chips in the Portainer catalog. Descriptive app categories, never internal enums.

status.description: Marks an entry build/import_registry.py wrote from a third-party registry and no person has finished. Its bench pack and peak_ram_mb may be null stubs and its prose is the importer's placeholder; the published catalog flags it as untested. A curated entry carries no status.

origin.description: Where an imported entry's compose file comes from, published with the entry: the registry, the entry's title there, the repository or registry the file is copied from, that source's licence and its copyright notice. It stays once a person finishes the entry.

licence.description: SPDX identifier. Only these permissive licences are imported; the importer reads this list.

attribution.description: The copyright lines of the source's licence file, or that file's address when it carries none.

pending.description: What a person still settles before an imported entry is curated: the findings the app checker and the catalog lint leave on its compose file, and the choices the importer cannot make. Only an imported entry carries it.

env_managed_keys.description: Keys the host's dashboard-sync re-injects into a running stack whenever they drift from what the panel renders (a rotated credential, a changed domain). In the public catalog they render to the operator-wired sentinel, never to a real value.

postgres_image_override.description: Only for an app whose upstream cannot run sources/_meta.json postgres_default_image.

s3_reconcile.description: Post-restore object-store consistency check. Report-only: it names the orphan rows, it never deletes them, because a bucket that is misconfigured looks exactly like a bucket that is empty.

service.description: Compose service the check runs inside.

user.description: User to exec as, when the app refuses to run its CLI as root.

check.description: Named check the ops side implements.

db_service.description: Compose service holding the index the check reads.

lifecycle.description: Commands the host runs inside one service around a schema change, and volumes it copies around an update of that service: the commands around every image update the update lane applies, the migration only when the update moves that service's image, and after a FORWARD restore once the database replay has put the snapshot's contents back. Declare it when the application keeps a schema its new code expects migrated (migrate), or when its new version upgrades state in a volume that the previous version then refuses or misreads (versioned_volumes); an entry declares one or both. A migration the application runs at container start is not enough on a restore: it runs against the pre-replay database and the replay then overwrites it. Every command is an argv array executed through docker exec, never a shell.

service.description: Compose service the commands run inside, and whose new version upgrades the versioned volumes.

user.description: User to exec as. Set it whenever a command writes into a volume the application later has to write itself, or the files come back owned by root.

migrate.description: The schema migration. Run in order, stopping at the first failure; a failure after an update rolls the image AND the database back.

before_update.description: Run in the RUNNING container just before the update lane deploys the new image (put the application into maintenance mode).

after_update.description: Run once the update settles, whether it was kept or rolled back (take the application out of maintenance mode).

ready.description: A command that exits 0 once the application can run the commands above. Before each phase of an update, the update lane runs it every few seconds until it succeeds, for up to timeout_seconds. Declare it when the image's entrypoint copies or upgrades the application before starting it: the container runs from the moment the entrypoint starts, and every command fails until the entrypoint is done. It has to succeed in the state before_update leaves the application in.

versioned_volumes.description: Named volumes the new version of the service upgrades in place and the previous version refuses to start on or misreads: the application's code tree, its configuration, its add-ons, or the database files it keeps in a volume (SQLite). The update lane copies each one before an update that moves the service, with the application in its backup mode when it declares one, and, when the update rolls back, puts the copy back with every service that mounts it stopped; what was written to the volume since the copy is lost, as a database dump's replay loses it. A volume of the users' files that the previous version still reads stays out, and so does one a database or a one-shot service mounts: a rollback does not stop either.

timeout_seconds.description: Ceiling for each command, database dump and replay, and volume copy and put-back.

pack.description: null only on an imported entry: it is in no bench pack.

quiesce.description: Commands the nightly maintenance runs inside one service around its backup, for an application whose live state a file-level snapshot can tear and the backup's own database dumps do not cover. Every command is an argv array executed through docker exec, never a shell. post must succeed when pre never ran: it runs after every backup attempt, after a resumed run and after a restore.

service.description: Compose service the commands run inside.

user.description: User to exec as, when the application refuses to run its CLI as root.

pre.description: Run in order before the backup, stopping at the first failure.

post.description: Run in order after the backup, whether it succeeded or not, stopping at the first failure.

peak_ram_mb.description: Required. The bench scheduler multiplies it by 1.15 to gate slot acquisition. null only on an imported entry, which is not measured yet.

env_required_when.description: Gates an env key on a SIBLING key being non-empty: {"RELAY_PASSWORD": "RELAY_HOST"} reads "the relay password is required only when a relay host is configured". Without it every optional credential is mandatory and the host's marketplace drops the whole template over a value nothing would read. The gate must name a key this template also defines.
